Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the fourth innings of the game and Sri Lanka's second innings. The West Indies players are out on the field, taking their respective positions. Sri Lanka skipper,  Dimuth Karunaratne, who has struggled for form in this series walks out with Lahiru Thirimanne who has had a much better time with the bat to open the innings. Kemar Roach is all set to operate with the new ball first up.

So Sri Lanka need 377 runs to win this game. One can rule that out scenario for the tourists unless there is a miracle. The visitors though will look to bat out the remaining overs of the day as their first mission before thinking about Day 5. West Indies will look to come out all guns blazing and try and get at least one or two wickets before the end of day's play. What is in store? Join us in a while for Sri Lanka's second innings.

A rather tough day so far for Sri Lanka. They were once again poor in the field as they dropped Brathwaite. To make matters worse, they were left a bowler short as Embuldeniya injured himself and had to be stretchered out. The hosts found themselves a bowler short which did affect them as Dhananjaya de Silva was forced to bowl a lot of overs but with no success. Vishwa Fernando too did not get any wicket. Lakmal once again impressed not just with his lines and lengths but with the heart he showed. He was rewarded with 2 wickets. Chameera too toiled hard and got two as well. A tough day on a flat pitch for the Sri Lankan bowlers.

West Indies started with 96 runs lead but once again John Campbell failed to deliver. Blackwood too failed to convert his start. Skipper, Brathwaite though continued from where he left off in the first innings, while Mayers continued his impressive run in Test cricket. The former was cautious while the latter raced his way to 55 in rather quick time. The pair added 82 runs and took the lead to 244. The skipper continued his merry ways while Holder took off from where Mayers left off. The skipper missed out on his ton by 15 runs but not before adding 87 with the former skipper and taking the lead over 300. After the departure of Brathwaite, Holder and Joshua Da Silva added some quickfire runs with their 53-run stand. In the process, Holder got his 10th Test fifty and took the lead over 375!

The declaration has finally arrived! It was a matter of when and it has finally come. Kraigg Brathwaite and co. are satisfied with the score they have got and will now look to end the day with a couple of wickets. Though many might feel the declaration could have come a bit earlier, Sri Lanka are not complaining as they now need to bat lesser duration than they might have anticipated but they still have a lot of time to bat.

We are back for the final session of the day. The Sri Lankan players are in a huddle, with their skipper having final words of motivation before they take the field. West Indies skipper, Kraigg Brathwaite walks out with Jason Holder to resume their innings. Dhananjaya de Silva set to start the session with the ball.
... Day 4, Evening Session ...

So, the lead right now reads 269. After what score will West Indies start feeling safe. How long will they take to dismiss Sri Lanka in the 4th innings? Will they declare in the final session? Or will they continue to bat and make sure Sri Lanka do not have any chance of going after the score? You never know what's in store. To find out, join us for the final session shortly.

It is another session where the bowlers had to toil hard on the deck which isn't offering a lot of assistance. Without their main spinner Embuldeniya, things have become tougher for the visitors. However, Lakmal and Chameera bowled really well.

A superb session for the hosts as they have piled on the runs with skipper Brathwaite leading from the front. The skipper has reached his half ton and looking set for a big score here. He got able support from Mayers who got out but not before playing a fine knock of 55 which came in just 76 balls. The southpaw took the chances and it paid off for him. After his wicket, Holder arrived and he went for the big shots. The former skipper along with the current skipper has swelled the lead to 269. It will be interesting to see how long these two bat in the final session of Day 4.

Review time! Kyle Mayers has been adjudged LBW. After a brief chat with Kraigg Brathwaite, he has decided to go for the review. Let's see if this works in Mayers' favor.

OUT! LBW! The review does not save Mayers but he does not take away a review with him either. A very good innings from Mayers comes to an end. Lakmal, the workhorse, gets his 11th wicket of the series. He has been a tireless worker and deserves all the success. Good length delivery pitching on off and coming in with the angle. Mayers looks to hit it across the line and pull it over mid-wicket. Mayers though misses his shot and gets hit on the front pad. A huge appeal follows and the umpire raises his finger. Mayers has a brief chat with Brathwaite and signals the 'T'. Replays roll in and first, Ultra Edge shows no involvement of bat. Time for the Ball Tracker. It shows the pitching to be in line, the impact to be in line, and the ball hits the top of middle stump. It is the umpire's call on wickets hitting. Not good enough to reverse the on-field call but good enough to retain the review.

Sri Lanka have got a couple of chances but they have failed to snaffle them. Chameera bowled his heart out and peppered Mayers with short stuff but he failed to get a reward. Mayers though has got the reward as he has taken the bowlers and raced to a half ton. Oshada put down a simple chance at short leg. So, West Indies have taken control here. They might change the gear soon and go for the quick runs. Interesting to see what target West Indies will be happy with.

Right! We are back for the 2nd session. Both the umpires take the field first and the Sri Lankan players follow them. West Indies captain Kraigg Brathwaite strides out along with Kyle Mayers to resume their innings. Dhananjaya de Silva to begin for Sri Lanka. One slip and one man at short leg in place. Here we go...
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

Sri Lanka head coach, Mickey Arthur, is caught for a chat before the 2nd session begins. Arthur says that a win is massive for them and they always go out to win. Tells winning is a process. Says their objective is to take wickets and contain the run rate. Adds they are looking to add more pressure. Says they cannot take a break with injuries. Tells he said the physio in the morning that they have not had an injury. Informs Embuldeniya is out of this game. Hopes Nissanka can come back soon.

Sri Lanka didn't bowl badly this session. They though gave away a few easy runs and failed to put consistent pressure on the West Indies batters from both ends. Lakmal once again was superb and provided them the breakthrough. Chameera bowled to plan and it worked when he got better off Blackwood. They would hope for more tight and tidy stuff in the post Lunch session. Join us for the same in a short while.

And then came the West Indies innings. Campbell fell early but Brathwaite continued. Along with Blackwood, the skipper added 44 and took the lead over 150. Blackwood departed playing a rash stroke and he would be mighty disappointed with the way he got dismissed. The wicket is looking really good for batting and the skipper will hope to put on a big partnership with Mayers in the 2nd session.

The day started 30 minutes prior to cover the lost overs on Day 3. West Indies took 23 balls to close the Lankan innings with Roach picking up 2 wickets. Nissanka did reach his 50 but couldn't continue as he fell trying to score quickly.

A decent session for West Indies. They knocked over the remaining 2 wickets quickly and then have reached 69 to extend their lead to 165. Brathwaite and Blackwood added 44 between them. The wicket of Blackwood means that Sri Lanka won't be too disappointed with their effort with the ball. We might see West Indies playing a bit more aggressively in the next session.

DRINKS! A good phase for West Indies. While they have lost Campbell for a low score, they have already added 36 more in their 96-run lead. Skipper Brathwaite and Blackwood are amidst a decent stand and would be eager to convert this one into a big one. For Sri Lanka, it is Lakmal who has provided them the breakthrough. Fernando has not bowled as tight as Sri Lanka would've liked. Also, Embuldeniya has injured himself and there is no news about him as of now. The way he was taken off, one might feel he may not bowl in this innings. So, Sri Lanka have a task in hand here.

He sends his partner back but Brathwaite is half way down. He returns. The throw from the deep comes at the bowler's end. Dimuth, the Lankan skipper though fails to collect the ball. Had he done that, Brathwaite was a goner. The ball eventually goes to the fence at deep extra cover.
